title: Senior RF Engineer
description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

You will be the technical authority for RF hardware behind Dedrone's airspace security products — the RF detection sensors that find and classify drones, and the countermeasure systems that defeat them. You own the hard RF problems end to end: wideband receive chains, high-power transmit chains, and their physical realization on board. You do not carry direct reports, but you technically lead a group of RF hardware engineers and antenna designers — you set the standards they design to, review their work, and grow their capability. This is a hands-on role. You will spend real time in simulation, on the bench, and in the chamber.

What You'll Do

Location: This role is based out of our Kassel office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.
Reports to: Director RF Engineering

  • Own RF front-end architecture from VHF through SHF: link budgets, frequency planning, spurious and intermodulation analysis, sensitivity and dynamic-range trade-offs.
  • Design and characterize mixers, high-power amplifiers, filters, and switching networks against demanding linearity, efficiency, and thermal targets.
  • Drive board-level simulation (EM, circuit, and co-simulation) and take designs through multi-layer RF PCB layout, stack-up definition, and fabrication release.
  • Lead bring-up, characterization, and design-for-test; close the loop between simulated and measured performance.
  • Set and enforce RF design standards, review checklists, and documentation practice across the group.
  • Mentor RF HW engineers and antenna designers; raise the technical bar through design reviews rather than rework.
  • Partner with DSP, software, mechanical, and systems engineering, and with regulatory/compliance on CE, FCC, and MIL-STD qualification.
  • Advise leadership on technology direction, build-vs-buy, and technical risk.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years in RF hardware design, with a track record of products shipped to volume.
  • Deep expertise across VHF, UHF, and SHF — not just one band.
  • Demonstrated design ownership of mixers and high-power amplifiers above 10 W.
  • Strong command of RF simulation tooling — EM and circuit solvers (e.g. ADS, AWR, HFSS, CST) — and the judgment to know when simulation is telling you the truth.
  • Multi-layer RF PCB design: controlled impedance, material selection, grounding, isolation, thermal management.
  • Fluent with VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and power measurement; comfortable debugging from first principles.
  • Proven technical leadership of a design group — setting direction and standards, mentoring, running rigorous design reviews.
  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Communications Engineering, or equivalent.

Nice to have

  • Antenna design and integration — element and array design, platform effects, radiation-pattern measurement.
  • Direction-finding techniques (amplitude/phase comparison, interferometry, TDOA, AoA estimation).
  • Beamforming across approaches: analog, digital, and hybrid; phased arrays and adaptive/null-steering methods.
  • Hands-on experience with SDR platforms.
  • Experience developing and qualifying products for regulated markets — CE, FCC, and/or MIL-STD.
  • Working knowledge of DSP concepts sufficient to trade functionality between analog and digital domains.

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

description:
About the team

Restaurants run on a stack of tools that rarely talk to each other: one for delivery, another for online orders, another for reservations, another for loyalty, and a till that knows nothing about any of them. The same guest can look like three different customers across three different systems.

DashOS is DoorDash's platform for fixing that. It connects marketplace ordering, direct ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management, marketing and point of sale around one shared view of the guest, so every product gets smarter as the others are used. DoorDash launched DashOS publicly at Dash Forward in September 2026, and from 2027 more than 80,000 restaurants on leading POS and middleware partners.

DashOS Engineering brings together engineers from across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt into one global organisation, led from London. Our teams cover reservations and guest CRM, digital ordering and omnichannel loyalty, POS and self-order kiosks, AI-powered marketing and Voice AI, and the shared data and integration platforms that connect them. Each team owns its own roadmap. The shared mission is making them work as one system.

About the role

We're looking for a backend-focused Software Engineer to build the high-performance, highly available services that restaurants depend on every day, from booking a table on a Friday night to recognising a regular the moment they order. You'll work closely with other engineers, product managers and designers, and because DashOS is newly launched, you'll help shape how its products connect rather than inheriting decisions someone else already made.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will...

  • Design, build, test, deploy and improve backend services for customer-facing features used by restaurants and their guests in markets around the world.
  • Own features end to end, from technical design through to launch and ongoing support, including taking part in an on-call rotation to keep systems reliable.
  • Work on hard problems in data, latency and scale: unifying guest identity across channels, real-time availability search across thousands of venues, and integrations with the systems restaurants already run.
  • Build on DoorDash's global platform, so the features you ship can reach restaurants across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt markets rather than being rebuilt for each one.
  • Work in a modern engineering environment with frequent daily releases, feature flags and AI coding agents used across code review, deployment and debugging.
  • Partner with engineers, product managers and designers across London and other DashOS locations to decide what to build and how.

We're excited about you because...

  • You have 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, and a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • You've built and operated backend services or web applications in production, with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms and system design.
  • You're fluent in at least one modern backend language (we mostly use Python), and you're happy to pick up new languages and tools as the platform evolves.
  • You care about the people using what you build, and you take ownership of technical solutions from first design to production.
  • You use AI coding tools as part of how you work, or you're keen to, and you're comfortable reviewing and taking responsibility for what they produce.
  • You enjoy collaborating with cross-functional teams to solve problems that don't have an obvious answer yet.

Tech you'll work with

Our services are built mainly in Python, with performance-critical systems in Rust, running on Google Cloud and DoorDash's global platform. AI coding agents are part of how we design, review and ship code, so we care more about how you solve problems than about which languages you've used before. You won't need to know every part of the stack on day one.

Where and how we work

This role is based in our London office at The River Building, on a hybrid pattern of 3 days a week in the office.

About SevenRooms

In 2011, Joel Montaniel, Allison Page, and Kinesh Patel founded SevenRooms after noticing that hospitality operators were missing a critical ingredient in the systems they were using to run their business: guest data. What began as a mission to help restaurants better understand and serve their guests evolved into a powerful platform used by merchants around the world.

With best-in-class tools for marketing, operations, and guest experience — all deeply integrated with its industry-leading CRM — SevenRooms empowers operators to drive revenue, streamline operations, and deliver experiences that keep guests coming back.

In 2025, DoorDash acquired SevenRooms to strengthen its in-store strategy and expand its merchant-first offerings. The combination brings together DoorDash’s scale, reach, and digital innovation with SevenRooms’ in-store capabilities to support hospitality businesses across every channel — from discovery and delivery to on-premise dining.

As DoorDash builds out its in-store capabilities, SevenRooms plays a central role in enabling merchants to grow their businesses and connect more meaningfully with guests, whether they’re ordering online or dining in. This move reflects DoorDash’s broader commitment to empowering local businesses, fostering stronger connections between consumers and the places they love, and building technology that meets merchants — and their customers — wherever they are.

Senior Engineer

Location: Bristol, London or Edinburgh (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: Senior Engineer II (TL1)

Team: Engineering

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Software Engineering Manager

 

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

 

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

 

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

 

What you’ll do

You’ll join a technology community of product-focused and data-led product and platform engineers working at scale. We have a diverse ecosystem, spanning TypeScript on AWS, Go on GCP and Scala, we index on product-minded problem solving over language purity.

As a Senior Engineer you’ll own a slice of the product end-to-end, from design through to production, and you’ll build AI coding agents as your default. We’re looking for someone whose judgement is worth more than their typing speed.

From your first day you’ll have paid access to Claude Code, with a budget we don’t ration, and access to the systems you need through MCP. Our tools and conventions evolve quickly, and you’ll directly impact how we build from here.

 

  • Own a slice of the product end to end: shape the problem with product and design, build the interface and the services behind it, ship it, and run it in production.
  • Work across the stack over time: depending on the team you’ll work across the interface people use, the services behind it, and the APIs between them, in whatever stack your team runs.
  • Build with AI coding agents as your default: Break work down so agents can execute, direct them, and review their output as carefully as you’d review a colleague’s pull request. You’ll also maintain the tests and safeguards that let agent written code merge safely.
  • Stay close to the people who use what you build: directly or through our forward-deployed engineers: a supplier’s operations team, a customer plugging in a car at night. Instrument what you ship so you can see how it’s used, and turn what you learn into shipped changes.
  • Make good work the default: shape the codebase, conventions and automated checks so that agents and new teammates produce the right thing without anyone catching it in review.
  • Mentor the team around you: Coach and mentor your peers and help improve how we work and evolve as a team. 

 

What you’ll bring

 

These are the practices and behaviours we see most in our top engineers and value deeply, but we don't expect everyone to tick every single box. If you're excited by the role and can see yourself thriving here, we’d love to hear from you.

  • Experience shipping production software: You have a depth of experience in either a front-end or back-end of a modern stack, and potentially an openness to stretch across both as you navigate our diverse ecosystem.
  • AI coding tools: You build with tools like Cursor or Claude Code, can walk us through work you’ve shipped this way and review AI output as rigorously as a colleague’s pull request.
  • Able to navigate a complex, high-stakes domain: You keep complex energy logic legible across microservices, knowing exactly when to use sync vs async to prevent cascading failures.
  • Cloud and operational ownership: You're comfortable deploying on major cloud platforms using shared tooling. You fully own your software in production, which includes participating in an out-of-hours on-call rota.
  • Strong product sense. You ask the “why” before building, and you can describe a time when user feedback or metrics changed what you shipped.
  • Clear written communication. You write specs, pull request descriptions and post-mortems with enough clarity and context that either a human teammate or an AI agent can immediately act on them.
  • A multiplier for your team: You mentor peers and proactively shape how the team works; introducing conventions, checks or shared context that makes everyone else’s output consistently better.

It would be great if you have

  • Experience building tooling around coding agents, such as MCP servers, skills or CI checks
  • Experience in energy, or another real-time or regulated field

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

 

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.
  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.
  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.
  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.
  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

 

Our Perks

 

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period
  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests
  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% of salary to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work
  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget
  • Climate: Access to Furthr, our climate action app

 

Come as you are

 

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

 

This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Legal Operations Specialist – Data Licensing on the IP & Licensing team, you will own the processes that let Mistral license content and data without slowing down. This role exists because we need someone who can turn legal analysis into repeatable workflows — managing rights, obligations, and restrictions across our growing dataset portfolio. You will work closely with the colleagues who negotiate our commercial and legal agreements, turning their work into clear metadata, tracked obligations, and automated systems.

Your impact will be visible in how smoothly data moves into our AI products: fewer bottlenecks, clearer rights status, and one reliable record for every data agreement we sign. You will sit where copyright, data protection, and AI meet, making sure that as we acquire and use training data, we comply with EU and US law, respect third-party rights, and enforce the restrictions our contracts impose. In scope: clearing permissions for inbound data, reviewing and codifying contracts, maintaining a central rights-and-obligations database, and building AI-powered workflows that make all of this scalable.

What You Will Do

  • Clear inbound data usage requests by researching rights status, scope, obligations, and restrictions — including anonymization and data protection requirements — before data enters our systems.

  • Review data-related agreements and codify their key terms into structured metadata, maintaining our template library and playbook alongside Legal.

  • Assess whether specific AI use cases fall within the scope of third-party agreements, flag gaps, and recommend contract amendments.

  • Build and maintain a central database that serves as the single source of truth for every signed data-related agreement.

  • Track and manage compliance with ongoing obligations — permitted uses, confidentiality, re-use rights — automate our reporting, and administer master licensing partnerships.

  • Verify provenance, ownership, and consent for acquired data, and identify obligations that require active monitoring.

  • Monitor that Mistral clients and partners stay within their granted rights, operating the approval system that enforces legal restrictions.

  • Design and run AI-powered workflows for contract review assistance, obligation extraction, and renewal alerts.

What We're Looking For

  • A bachelor's degree in law, publishing, information science, business, or a related field.

  • 2–5 years of experience in copyright, permissions, licensing, legal operations, or contract administration — ideally in an AI, tech, or data-driven environment.

  • Working knowledge of EU and US copyright law and contract administration, with demonstrated ability to interpret contracts independently.

  • Meticulous attention to detail and discretion with confidential contracts, combined with strong project-management skills.

  • Clear, direct communication and the initiative to anticipate needs through ambiguity.

  • A legal-ops mindset: you want to turn legal analysis into repeatable, scalable processes, not just handle one-off reviews.

  • Comfort building agentic AI workflows in a complex enterprise environment — you are an AI power user, ideally with experience setting up such workflows in a legal team.

  • Additional depth in formal legal training, CLM platforms (e.g., Ironclad), publishing-house contracts, or European languages (French, German, Spanish, etc.) is welcome.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

About the role

The Partner Engagements Manager, Compliance Strategy will lead Checkout’s external-facing compliance strategy across banking, scheme and other strategic partner relationships.

You will own the operating model and delivery of compliance-related partner engagements, including annual reviews, periodic due diligence, requests for information, licensing and scheme initiatives, and readiness for product or geographic expansion. You will ensure that Checkout presents a consistent, accurate and well-evidenced view of its compliance framework, while converting external expectations into practical improvements to our roadmap, controls, processes and operating model.

The role combines strategic ownership, senior stakeholder management and hands-on delivery. You will lead complex engagements, advise Compliance leadership, build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, and develop the partner-engagement capability of the team, including managing and coaching Senior Analyst(s) as the structure is established.

What you will do

  • Own the Compliance Strategy partner-engagement portfolio, prioritising work across banking partners, schemes and other strategic external stakeholders.

  • Establish and continuously improve the operating model for partner engagements, including governance, roles and responsibilities, service standards, evidence expectations, response libraries, escalation routes and management information.

  • Lead annual KYC AML partner compliance reviews, partner onboarding or refreshes, complex RFIs and other material external engagements from planning through to closure.

  • Act as a senior Compliance representative in partner meetings, with high level input around Checkout’s compliance framework, risk management approach, policies, controls, governance and improvement plans with clarity and confidence.

  • Provide oversight and challenge to response packs, control narratives, policy summaries, presentations and supporting evidence, ensuring consistency, accuracy and appropriate ownership.

  • Lead compliance support for scheme, product-launch and geographic-expansion initiatives, ensuring external partner obligations and readiness requirements are identified, tracked and addressed.

  • Translate partner feedback, requests and emerging expectations into strategic recommendations, roadmap priorities, control enhancements and process improvements.

  • Build strong working relationships across Compliance, Legal, Risk, Product, Operations, Commercial, Finance, Technology and regional teams to align delivery and resolve dependencies.

  • Maintain clear governance over engagement risks, issues, decisions, action plans and remediation, escalating material matters to the Head of Compliance Strategy and relevant governance forums.

  • Produce concise and decision-useful updates for Compliance leadership, senior management and governance committees, including themes, trends, risks, commitments and delivery status.

  • Partner with relevant second-line teams to ensure external engagement activity is consistent with the Compliance framework, risk appetite, regulatory obligations and the responsibilities of the three lines of defence.

  • Coach, develop and set clear expectations for Senior Analyst(s).

  • Create and implement a high-quality, scalable and collaborative partner-engagement framework.

  • Identify opportunities to use better data, tooling, workflow design and documentation to improve response quality, reduce duplication and increase the resilience of the Compliance operating model.

  • Represent Compliance Strategy in cross-functional strategic initiatives and take on other priorities that support long-term capability maturation.

What you will need to be successful

  • Typically 3–5 years of experience in a similar role within compliance, regulatory compliance, risk, audit, legal or a related function in payments, fintech, banking or another regulated financial-services environment.

  • Demonstrable experience leading external partner, banking, scheme, audit, regulatory or due-diligence engagements.

  • Experience translating regulatory or partner expectations into practical requirements, delivery plans, governance and measurable improvements.

  • Experience leading complex, cross-functional workstreams with multiple stakeholders, dependencies and deadlines.

  • Experience coaching or managing people, setting priorities, giving feedback and creating clarity in a fast-moving environment.

  • Strong understanding of the payments ecosystem and the compliance expectations relevant to banking partners, payment schemes and regulated financial institutions.

  • Working knowledge of relevant compliance domains such as AML/CTF, sanctions, KYC/CDD/EDD, licensing, safeguarding, operational resilience, regulatory change or control assurance.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present complex issues, defend recommendations and influence senior stakeholders.

  • Strong judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively, distinguish material from non-material issues and escalate appropriately.

  • Strong organisational, analytical and project-management skills, with a track record of delivering high-quality outcomes under pressure.

  • ICA, ACAMS or another relevant professional qualification is desirable.

How you will work at Checkout

  • Be The Owner: Set direction, create accountability and ensure commitments are delivered.

  • Talk Straight: Give clear, evidence-led advice and communicate difficult messages respectfully and early.

  • One Team: Build alignment across functions and regions, sharing context and bringing people with you.

  • No Room for Approximation: Set a high bar for accuracy, evidence, consistency and regulatory defensibility.

  • Athlete Mindset: Plan rigorously, raise the standard and keep improving the capability of the function.

  • Better Every Day: Turn recurring engagement friction into scalable processes, tools and operating-model improvements.

  • Pace Matters: Balance urgency with thoughtful risk judgement and disciplined execution.

  • Fundamentally Positive: Lead with trust, humility and a practical, solution-oriented approach.

What success looks like

  • Partner engagement framework is clearly documented with detailed SLAs and communicated to all relevant stakeholders.

  • Partner engagements are planned, governed and delivered consistently across the portfolio.

  • Checkout is represented externally through clear, accurate, credible and coherent compliance narratives.

  • Material risks, gaps and commitments are visible to the right stakeholders and managed through to resolution.

  • Scheme, product and geographic-expansion initiatives receive timely and practical Compliance Strategy support.

  • Partner feedback is converted into measurable improvements in processes, documentation, monitoring, tooling and capability.

  • The Senior Analyst(s) and wider stakeholder network have clear priorities, effective ways of working and opportunities to grow.

  • Compliance leadership has reliable management information to understand engagement themes, risks, capacity and progress.

title: Composite Development Engineer
description: We are looking for a Composite Development Engineer to build the material foundation of our rocket structures and generate material data that design and analysis can trust. You will work across material selection, process development, specimen preparation, laboratory testing, and component validation. Your work will ensure that material properties are measured on the materials we use, made with the processes we intend to employ, and suitable for real engineering decisions. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, have just crossed €10m in revenue for our first operating year and are applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Define material requirements based on system, component, manufacturing, and structural interfaces. Select composite material systems and qualify suitable manufacturing processes. Plan and run coupon-level characterisation campaigns, from specimen preparation and testing through to usable design values. Develop and characterise new material systems and processing methods. Validate material properties on manufactured components and feed results back into design and analysis. Help develop the materials laboratory, including procedures, safety practices, equipment capability, and material-handling standards. What we are looking for A Master’s degree or PhD in materials science, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline. Two to five years of experience working with composite materials; strong student-team experience will also be considered. Genuine enjoyment of practical laboratory work, including specimen preparation, testing, and fixture troubleshooting. Experience handling resins and chemicals safely, with the ability to develop procedures where they do not yet exist. A methodical approach to experimental work, measurement, documentation, and data quality. Fluent English and the ability to communicate technical results clearly. Desirable experience Carbon-fibre materials, resin systems, prepregs, laminates, or other aerospace composites. Composite test standards, including ASTM, ISO, or equivalent methods. Laboratory equipment such as DSC, DMA, tensile-test systems, microscopy, or similar materials-characterisation equipment. Working proficiency in German. description: About GiveDirectly What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need? Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid. Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty? We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join. We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. raw.jobDescription:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

About this role:

Are you an experienced engineer at the stage of your career where, above all, you want to do good?

This role is about using engineering to support fundraising: delighting our donors; helping our fundraisers; getting donations recorded and safely started on their journey to our recipients; telling donors and the public about what happens to their gifts. A bit of website development. A lot of plumbing.

The good news about this position:

  • You will make a difference to people in extreme poverty
  • You will work independently, with few constraints
  • You will work directly with lovely people from across our fundraising teams

The trade-offs:

  1. There is only one other fundraising engineer and mostly you will be working on your own
  2. Our technology is a mixture of boring (Laravel, PHP, plain JS, HTML and CSS) and legacy (Salesforce, Wordpress, wrangling CSV files sent by our partners)
  3. We're growing, but this is a role for someone who values depth and impact over a fast title ladder.

The maybe good maybe bad news about the role depending on who you are:

  • We are all in on AI where it allows us to get more $ to people in extreme poverty

If you want a role where you will be part of a bigger engineering team, working in Python or working on more complex tasks, then please take a look at our other engineering roles.

This role is right for you if:

  • You care about our mission
  • You agree with our values
  • You have the right to work in one of the countries we're able to hire from (you can check the current list here).
  • You're happy working remotely, and taking meetings across East Africa Time and US Eastern Time.
  • You are happy to travel to meet your colleagues in the US, Europe and Africa a few weeks a year
  • You are fluent in English
  • You have 4+ years of engineering experience
  • You're happy working autonomously: defining what needs doing, doing it, getting it tested and launched, fixing the bugs, and hustling to make progress every day.
  • You're comfortable being on-call on peak donation days (Giving Tuesday and the last weeks of the year), including owning an incident: working out what matters, communicating with fundraisers, and debugging on legacy and others' code, sometimes when no other engineers are available.
  • You are happy with our boring and legacy technologies (Laravel, PHP, plain JS, HTML, CSS, Salesforce, Wordpress, SQL, wrangling csv files etc). You don’t have to be experienced in all of them, but you do have to be genuinely happy to use them (many engineers are not…).
  • You are happy and skilled at working directly with non-engineers on messy, poorly defined, rapidly changing, sometimes boring tasks

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

United States

  • Base Salary: $181,130
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 15% (~$27,170, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization's current performance multiplier, this amount would be ~$31,789 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $208,300+
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: $21,393

United Kingdom

  • Base Salary: £124,370
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 15% (~£18,656, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization's current performance multiplier, this amount would be ~£21,827 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: £143,026+
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: £2,760

Kenya

  • Base Salary: $112,350
  • Bonus at Target Performance: 15% (~$16,853, with potential for upside. For reference, with the organization's current performance multiplier, this amount would be ~$19,717 in 2025)
  • Estimated Total Compensation at Target: $129,203+
  • Annual Benefits Stipend: $8,453

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in the US, UK or Kenya, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Why work at GiveDirectly?

At GiveDirectly, we work to ensure that you have everything you need to excel in your role and on your team, including:

  • A positive and supportive team with opportunities for advancement
  • A demonstrated commitment to helping all staff develop and grow
  • A competitive salary, including bonus
  • A robust health benefits plan (exact details will vary by country)
  • Unlimited PTO (that we encourage staff to take!)
  • Desk allowance and flexible work location

About this specific hiring process

  • Take-home coding assignment
  • Live Coding (60 mins)
  • Systems Design (60 mins)
  • Project Deep Dive + Behavioral (60 mins)

*It’s possible that there will be adjustments to this interview process. Any changes will be communicated to you during the process.

#LI-REMOTE

Working at GiveDirectly

GiveDirectly is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing, reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

Reasonable Accommodations

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible work environment. If you require any accommodations during the application or interview process, or to perform the essential functions of the role, please email us at careers@givedirectly.org with the email subject “Accommodation Needed”. We will work with you to ensure reasonable accommodations are made to support your needs.

Want to put your best foot forward on your GiveDirectly application? Take a look at our Candidate Application Prep Guide!

Referrals

title: Senior Platform Engineer
description:
Senior Platform Engineer 

À propos du rôle et de l'équipe

La Cloud Platform Engineering (CPE) est une Business Unit de près de 200 personnes qui continue de se renforcer pour accompagner les ambitions tech de Decathlon. Notre objectif principal est de rationaliser le catalogue de produits techniques et de fournir des services clé en main pour les équipes IT, afin de leur permettre de se concentrer sur le développement de fonctionnalités à fort impact applicatif.

Au sein de la CPE, tu rejoindras l'équipe Cloud Dev. Notre mission est de fournir des fonctionnalités essentielles et abstraites pour le Cloud, en appliquant les meilleures pratiques de développement d'ingénierie logicielle pour unifier, sécuriser et optimiser nos plateformes.

Tu rejoindras une équipe à taille humaine, composée d'ingénieurs passionnés. Nous sommes fans de développement logiciel, d'Infrastructure as Code, de culture DevOps/SRE, d'automatisation, de veille technologique... et bien sûr, de sport !

Périmètre et missions d'un Platform Engineer

En tant que Platform Engineer, tu joueras un rôle central dans l'autonomisation des équipes de développement grâce à l'ingénierie de plateforme. Tes missions s'articuleront autour des piliers suivants :

1. Ingénierie Logicielle & Abstraction Cloud

description:
At IMC, technology is not a department; it’s at the heart of everything we do. Developed in house, our innovative software makes millions of trading decisions daily, and we win by making better and faster decisions than our competition.

IMC’s Amsterdam-based Global VMM Data team works on a centralised global data platform to serve high-quality curated data for Valuation Market Making (VMM) research and strategies all throughout IMC. We address the ever changing data requirements and our team tries to solve this in a young project building a central system to ingest, curate and expose data to our research tooling within IMC.

Your Core Responsibilities:

As a Trading Data Software Engineer, you'll work on enabling high-quality research using fundamental option pricing data. Next to that you will increase researchers' focus by centralising the curation of the data and enable quick onboarding of new data sets, to allow for researching new types of strategies that are going to play a vital role in the strategies of IMC now and in the future. We build the tooling that allows a team of data curators to perform their magic and on top of that we expose our data to research tooling to provide a global access.

You’ll write reliable, high-performance software while balancing time to production with quality and testability. Advanced automated testing and daily deployments will allow you to achieve agile and incremental benefits. Within the complex landscape of IMC and its systems and technologies, you’ll be constantly challenged to consider trade-offs between latency, throughput, simplicity, scalability and maintainability. Your core tasks will include:

  • Coding, developing, testing, deploying and maintaining applications and automations for data curators, other VMM developers and Traders/researchers to support them and understand their actual needs and the data we serve them.
  • Working on a young project and being involved of the architectural design of our system.
  • Building a system that is highly-performant at serving petabytes of data globally.

Your Skills and Experience:

  • At least > 4 years of experience as a Software Engineer 
  • Strong programming skills in Java (11+), but experience in the latest versions of Java is highly desirable
  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes and Linux
  • Strong programming skills with Python, especially around data - highly preferred
  • Experience working in data analysis and building out data platforms and data - highly preferred
  • The ability able to work under minimal supervision and to take full ownership of the applications you build
  • Strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills; ability to solve problems creatively and proactively
  • Prior knowledge of trading / capital markets is not required. Curiosity and a willingness to learn is.

Our tech stack includes an ever-evolving range of systems and technologies, and our engineers have the freedom to choose the best solution for the problem at hand. If a new technology has the potential to add value, we’ll actively invest in exploring, adopting and developing it. 

About Us

IMC is a research-driven trading firm where quantitative modeling, machine learning, and engineering shape how modern markets are traded. A stabilizing force in markets since 1989, we provide liquidity across trading venues, delivering the best outcome in value and risk management to investors. Using our own technology and capital, we build proprietary systems and algorithms that operate across global markets. Our researchers, traders, and engineers work as a collective, combining rapid experimentation, advanced infrastructure, and real-time feedback to turn insight into execution and execution into advantage.

  • A collaborative approach and a desire to learn and develop within a fast-paced agency environment.

Ogilvy celebrates its people. Fully. Enthusiastically. Unhesitatingly. We’ll empower you with the tools you’ll need to succeed. We’ll give you the autonomy to seek out new paths and better ways of doing things. We’ll support you with colleagues who are experts in their disciplines, drawn from across the Ogilvy network. Mark43’s mission is to empower communities and their governments with new technologies that improve the safety and quality of life for all. We build powerful, scalable, and elegant software that sets a new standard for the tools upon which our first responders rely. Our users are diverse, and we are therefore committed to embracing diversity of thought and experience within our team. 

Our platform is already trusted by major public safety agencies across North America—including Boston, D.C., Seattle, and the California Highway Patrol—and we’ve expanded into the UK. 

Now, we’re entering an exciting new chapter: Mark43 is building a next-generation AI-augmented engineering team. This is a foundational opportunity to help rethink how software is designed, developed, and delivered using intelligent agentic or related tools. 

What You’ll Do 

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to help lead our AI-enabled engineering initiative. You’ll work at the frontier of AI and software development, experimenting with agentic workflows and shaping how AI tools are integrated into every layer of our engineering stack. 

This isn’t just about using AI to autocomplete code—it’s about designing and orchestrating systems of AI agents that can plan, write, review, test, and deploy software collaboratively. In essence, you’ll play a role akin to a tech lead for a team of intelligent coding agents. 

You will: 

  • Design multi-agent systems with coding-focused agents (e.g., code writer, reviewer, tester, deployer) 
  • Write the prompts, logic, and scaffolding that guide each agent’s behavior 
  • Handle tool use, like enabling agents to access the file system, test runners, version control, and internal APIs 
  • Evaluate and refine agents’ output, performance, collaboration patterns, and feedback loops 

If you were on the team last week, you might have: 

  • Prototyped a new coding assistant workflow using open-source LLMs and internal knowledge bases 
  • Led an architecture discussion on agentic build pipelines or automated PR generation 
  • Collaborated with a cross-functional team to build a fast, AI-powered interface for internal tooling 
  • Helped define the evaluation framework for AI contributions—accuracy, speed, and impact 
  • Mentored a teammate on combining TypeScript and AI tools to accelerate UI prototyping 
  • Explored best practices for safely and securely integrating generative AI into a public sector codebase 
  • Participated in our on call rotation 

 

What You’ll Need 

We’re looking for an experienced software engineer who is eager to build smarter systems by pairing technical expertise with emerging AI tools. You don’t need to be an AI researcher—but you do need hands-on experience applying generative AI tools to real-world development workflows. 

You should have: 

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience 
  • Proficiency with at least part of our stack: Java, TypeScript + React, and MySQL 
  • Extensive applied experience with AI-assisted development tooling—whether it’s Cursor, Windsurf, LLM APIs, codegen platforms, vector databases, agentic frameworks like LangChain, or custom-built systems 
  • A strong product mindset and interest in building for real-world impact 
  • A bias toward experimentation, iteration, and continuous learning 
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and helping define best practices in a rapidly evolving space 

We’re flexible on which tools you’ve used—we care more about your ability to learn, adapt, and creatively apply AI in practical settings than checking a specific tech box.  

People Who Thrive on Our Team Also Tend to Be: 

  • Humble, open, and curious. You ask questions and seek to understand before making assumptions 
  • Collaborative by default. You believe the best outcomes come from shared knowledge and ownership 
  • Mission-driven. You care about building tech that serves the public good 
  • Comfortable with uncertainty. You’re energized by open problems and emerging technologies 
  • Growth-oriented. You embrace feedback, learn from setbacks, and look for ways to get better every day

title: Managing Director - THG Studios
description:
About THG Ingenuity 

THG Ingenuity is a proprietary Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) technology, robotics, and operations platform built for global ecommerce. Developed through more than two decades of operating ecommerce and retail services at scale, its software and automation capabilities have been engineered, tested, and refined through the real-world demands of managing complex commerce operations. Today, THG Ingenuity provides an integrating operating environment that enables brands to intelligently optimise the entire commerce lifecycle from browsing and checkout to AI inventory management and forecasting, automated fulfilment, carrier control, and customer experience. The platform comprises: 

  • THG Fulfil: The fulfilment operating system for global ecommerce. Delivered via a proprietary SaaS and Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model, THG Fulfil orchestrates every stage of checkout, fulfilment, delivery, and customer experience through an integrated system. 
  • THG Studios: The UK's most innovative creative hub, helping brands create content that connects, experiences that engage, and IP that scales, all from its end-to-end, in-house facilities.  
  • THG Commerce: A cloud-native technology stack enabling retailers and brands to create intelligent, AI-powered, digital shopping experiences, while integrated marketplace and social commerce functionality allows brands to reach customers across every sales channel 

With its expertise in building and scaling brands, THG Ingenuity is uniquely positioned to bring pertinent, pragmatic, and global know-how across all aspects of commerce. 

Managing Director - THG Studios 

Reporting to: Group CEO 

About THG Studios 

THG Studios is an integrated creative and production agency helping ambitious brands create high-quality content, build stronger connections with their audiences and deliver measurable growth. 

Based in Manchester, we bring creative, production and technology together under one roof. Our work spans high-volume e-commerce content, social-first campaigns, brand platforms, immersive experiences and technology-led activations. 

We work with a broad range of well-known brands, including Disney, L’Oréal, Myprotein, LOOKFANTASTIC, ASDA, Sky Vegas, Warner Bros., Jet2, Swizzels, Avolta and The Overlap. 

As THG Studios continues to grow, we are looking for an ambitious and commercially focused Managing Director to lead the agency and build on its strong creative, production and technology capabilities. 

The Role 

The Managing Director will set the strategic direction for THG Studios and take overall accountability for its growth, commercial performance and market position. 

With full P&L ownership, you will be responsible for delivering sustainable revenue and profit growth, developing the agency’s proposition and identifying new opportunities across existing clients, new business and strategic partnerships. 

You will lead and support the senior leadership team, including the Group Creative Director, General Managers and Client Partners. You will also play an active role in senior client relationships, major pitches, strategic opportunities and escalated matters. 

This role requires a proven leader from the creative, production, content or agency sector who understands how to grow a successful business. You will need to combine commercial focus with creative ambition, strong operational discipline and the ability to build a high-performing team. 

Key Responsibilities 

Strategy and growth 

  • Set the strategic direction for THG Studios and lead the delivery of its growth plan. 
  • Identify new markets, sectors, services, partnerships and revenue opportunities. 
  • Develop and strengthen THG Studios’ agency proposition and competitive position. 
  • Build on the agency’s existing capabilities to increase its value to clients and unlock new commercial opportunities. 
  • Ensure growth plans are focused, measurable and aligned with the businesses wider objectives. 

Commercial and P&L ownership 

  • Take full ownership of the THG Studios P&L and deliver agreed revenue and profit targets. 
  • Drive sustainable growth across existing client accounts, new business and strategic partnerships. 
  • Ensure strong commercial discipline across pricing, margins, forecasting and client profitability. 
  • Make informed decisions about investment in people, technology and capabilities to support growth. 
  • Monitor commercial performance and take action where performance is not on track. 

Client leadership and new business 

  • Be ultimately accountable for client retention, account growth and new business performance. 
  • Lead and support the Client Partners and Business Development team, who will manage day-to-day client and new business activity. 
  • Maintain senior relationships with key clients and become involved in strategic accounts, major opportunities and escalated matters. 
  • Support or lead significant pitches, tenders, negotiations and partnership opportunities. 
  • Ensure the agency is consistently identifying opportunities to increase its share of client spend. 

Leadership and market position 

  • Set clear strategic priorities, accountabilities and measures of success across the agency. 
  • Ensure the leadership team is aligned behind the growth strategy and equipped to deliver it. 
  • Build a high-performing, commercially focused culture centred on growth, creativity and client value. 
  • Raise the profile of THG Studios within the creative, production and wider marketing industry. 
  • Represent THG Studios with senior clients, partners and stakeholders. 
  • Build relationships that strengthen the agency’s reputation, reach and access to new opportunities. 

About You 

You will be an experienced senior leader from a creative agency, production company, content business, media organisation or related environment, with a proven track record of delivering growth. You will have experience of: 

  • Growing revenue and profitability across an agency, production or creative services business. 
  • Developing and delivering a clear growth strategy, with evidence of achieving measurable results. 
  • Winning new clients, expanding existing accounts and increasing share of client spend. 
  • Identifying new markets, services, partnerships and commercial opportunities. 
  • Building or repositioning an agency proposition to strengthen its competitive position. 
  • Taking full P&L ownership and making sound commercial decisions around pricing, margins, investment and profitability. 
  • Leading senior teams through periods of growth, change or business development. 
  • Building strong relationships with senior clients and stakeholders. 
  • Leading major pitches, tenders, negotiations and strategic partnerships. 
  • Understanding the creative and production market, including changing client expectations, technology and new ways of working. 
  • Combining commercial ambition with a strong understanding of creative quality and client value. 
  • Communicating a clear vision and bringing people with you. 

You will be commercially ambitious, credible and confident, with the energy and judgement to identify opportunities, convert them into growth and build a sustainable, high-performing business. 

THG Ingenuity is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you are invited to interview, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to the recruitment process that will enable you to perform to the best of your ability.

THG Ingenuity is committed to creating a diverse & inclusive environment and hence welcomes applications from all sections of the community.

Because of the high volumes of applications our opportunities attract, it sometimes takes us time to review and consider them all. We endeavour to respond to every application we receive within 14 days. If you haven't heard from us within that time frame or should you have any specific questions about this or other applications for positions at THG Ingenuity please contact one of our Talent team to discuss further.

  • Android Studio 

  • Git 

  • Experience owning production Android applications

  • Actively using AI throughout your development workflow 

  • Interest / understanding / experience in cross-platform development

  • Kotlin Multiplatform 

  • VoIP or real-time communication 

  • Analytics and observability tooling (Mixpanel, Crashlytics or similar) 

  

Who You Are  

  • You naturally take ownership without waiting for permission. 

  • You enjoy solving hard technical problems while thinking about the bigger picture. 

  • You care deeply about software craftsmanship and user experience. 

  • You can explain the trade-offs behind your technical choices 

  • You enjoy partnering with product teams and learning directly from customer feedback. 

  • You share what you know and help others improve and become stronger. 

  • You're pragmatic. You know when perfection matters and when shipping matters more. 

  • You're excited about building software that genuinely changes people's lives. 

  • You're based in or around Amsterdam and able to come to our office two to three times a week 

What You Get  

Competitive compensation  

  • 80,000 - 85,000 euros per year all-in gross

Learning and growth  

  • €1,500 annual personal development budget, plus access to company-wide training sessions to keep learning and evolving.  

Time to recharge  

  • 25 vacation days

Work from anywhere

A team you’ll actually want to be part of  

  • Weekly team lunch every Thursday

description: Bij Dyflexis helpen we wereldwijd miljoenen medewerkers met onze workforce management software. Van de bakker om de hoek tot internationale hotel- en retailketens. De software is krachtig, de vragen van klanten zijn divers, en geen dag is hetzelfde. Je leert het product door en door kennen en draagt bij aan iets dat in meer dan 20 landen hard groeit. Dat doen we door snel te werken, met korte lijntjes, zonder onnodige vergaderingen en zonder politiek. Ownership, heldere communicatie en samen dingen voor elkaar krijgen, daar draait het bij ons om. We leren al doende en blijven continu verbeteren in hoe we onze klanten helpen. In deze rol betekent dat vooral: jij bent de eigenaar van onze cijfers. Je houdt de administratie van een snelgroeiend SaaS-bedrijf strak en betrouwbaar, en je maakt het proces elke maand een stukje slimmer. Dit ga je doen Als Senior Finance Administrator run je de volledige financiële administratie, van factuur tot jaarrekening. Je sluit zelfstandig de maand, het kwartaal en het jaar af. Je werkt nauw samen met Sales, Customer Success en het management team, vertaalt financiële vraagstukken naar heldere afspraken en kijkt steeds waar handwerk eruit kan. Je voert de volledige financiële administratie en verzorgt zelfstandig de maand-, kwartaal- en jaarafsluiting, inclusief reconciliaties, accruals en overlopende posten. Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor facturatie en debiteurenbeheer, verwerkt abonnementsomzet (deferred revenue) correct en levert input voor rapportages en SaaS-KPI’s zoals MRR, ARR en DSO. Je verzorgt de btw-aangiftes (inclusief ICP), bewaakt de fiscale compliance en bereidt de jaarrekening voor. Je verbetert en automatiseert processen tussen Dyflexis, Salesforce en Twinfield, zodat onze data altijd betrouwbaar, volledig en snel beschikbaar is. Je bewaakt interne controles zoals autorisaties, het vier-ogenprincipe en betaalrondes, en signaleert risico’s voordat ze een probleem worden. Dit heb je nodig 5+ jaar ervaring in een financiële functie binnen een SaaS omgeving (bijvoorbeeld Accountancy of Finance & Control). Aantoonbare ervaring met zelfstandige maand- en jaarafsluitingen, goede kennis van btw-wetgeving. Sterk in Excel en snel thuis in meerdere systemen. Ervaring met Twinfield is een plus. Je zet AI al slim in je werk in, van het verwerken van facturen tot reconciliaties en rapportages. Handmatig werk dat geautomatiseerd kan worden, laat jij niet liggen. Nauwkeurig, gestructureerd en stressbestendig rond deadlines. Knelpunten los je structureel op, niet met een pleister. Vloeiend Nederlands en Engels (C1), Duits is een sterke pre. Dit krijg je er voor terug - Bij Dyflexis maak je deel uit van een ambitieus, energiek en klantgericht team. Wij bieden: - Een vast salaris tot €4,500 bruto per maand op basis van een 40-urige werkweek (afhankelijk van ervaring). - Persoonlijk opleidingsbudget om je vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen. - 25 vakantiedagen plus een vrije dag op je verjaardag, in ruil voor taart. - Onze eigen chef-kok die je dagelijks verrast met een verse lunch. - De leukste feestjes, borrels en tripjes (wintersport, Ibiza en meer). - Lidmaatschap bij ARJ Training (de sportschool van kampioenen Tarik en Levi Rigters). - Een solide pensioenregeling en 8% vakantiegeld. - Vakantiedagen kopen of verkopen, jij bepaalt. - Reiskostenvergoeding en een thuiswerkvergoeding. - Elke vrijdag een heerlijke stoelmassage om je weekend mee te beginnen. Apply now Wil jij de cijfers van een hard groeiend SaaS-bedrijf zelf in handen hebben? Druk op de blauwe knop! Een motivatiebrief is niet nodig. description: ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE : École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation. Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être. IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient. IMT Mines Albi, au travers du Centre Génie Industriel (CGI), développe des recherches à la frontière entre l’intelligence artificielle et le génie industriel, en collaboration avec des partenaires publics et industriels nationaux et internationaux. Le Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) ( https://cgi.imt-mines-albi.fr/ ) compte environ 70 personnes dont 25 doctorants. Le centre s’intéresse à l’accompagnement de la transition des écosystèmes en permettant de prendre des décisions responsables et durables, dans des environnements instables ou perturbés. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés. Le CGI est structuré selon des axes de recherche appliquée et des programmes scientifiques. Les axes de recherche appliquée sont : Axe FLOWS : Flexible Logistics and Operations for sustainable WorldS dans lequel ce poste est rattaché . Axe DiSCS : Digital Systems for Crisis management and Security ; Axe TRACE : Territorial Resilience, Agility, and Circular Economy ; Axe WHOPS : Well-being and Health through Organizational Processes and Services . Les deux programmes scientifiques au cœur de ces axes de recherche sont : HOPOPOP : Hybridization for Operations & Planning, Organizations & Performance, Optimization & Problem-solving ; AIME-DM : Automated Information Modeling and Extraction for Decision-Makers . DESCRIPTION DU POSTE : Dans le contexte de l’Education 4.0, les différents acteurs d’un établissement de formation universitaire (étudiants, personnels, intervenants extérieurs, etc.) ont des contraintes et des objectifs différents ce qui rend complexe la coordination et le pilotage de tels établissements (organisation et planification des enseignements, gestion des espaces collectifs, organisation des sessions d’examens…). En complément, ces établissements doivent s’adapter tant sur la gestion de leurs sites (meilleure adéquation à de nouvelles formes pédagogiques) que sur les flux de personnes les utilisant pour une meilleure répartition des charges et une interopérabilité de tous les outils à disposition (par exemple, un gestionnaire d’emploi du temps). Dans ce cadre, le jumeau numérique organisationnel représente le système qui permet une simulation et une aide à la prise de décision par des échanges bidirectionnels entre l’organisation physique (personnes et systèmes dont les bâtiments) et sa réplique virtuelle dans un objectif de pilotage global des flux. Le projet DIGIFAC’Santé s’inscrit dans ce contexte. Il porte sur la conception et le développement d'un jumeau numérique des sites d’une université, de la gestion des flux étudiants et personnels et de l’évolution pédagogique de ses formations. Un jumeau numérique ne peut remplir son rôle qu'à la condition de représenter fidèlement les informations essentielles à la prise de décision, elles-mêmes issues de données collectées dans les différents services de l’Université et des applications logicielles actuelles. Or, ces applications présentent des niveaux d’hétérogénéité différents selon leurs fonctionnalités. La nature des opérations réalisées (emploi du temps, gestion des salles et du matériel, etc.) impose des contraintes fortes sur la disponibilité de ces données : leur collecte automatique et en temps réel n'est pas toujours techniquement envisageable, ce qui constitue un défi central pour l'alimentation du jumeau numérique. L’étude à mener dans le cadre de ce projet vise à : Modéliser le besoin informationnel . Il s'agit de concevoir un méta-modèle capable de représenter, de façon générique et formelle, les informations strictement nécessaires à l’alimentation du jumeau numérique universitaire. Alimenter les modèles . Une fois le méta-modèle du besoin informationnel établi, la question de son instanciation à partir de données réelles des applications existantes se pose. ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE :

École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation.

Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être.

IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient.

IMT Mines Albi, au travers du Centre Génie Industriel (CGI), développe des recherches à la frontière entre l’intelligence artificielle et le génie industriel, en collaboration avec des partenaires publics et industriels nationaux et internationaux.

Le Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) (https://cgi.imt-mines-albi.fr/) compte environ 70 personnes dont 25 doctorants. Le centre s’intéresse à l’accompagnement de la transition des écosystèmes en permettant de prendre des décisions responsables et durables, dans des environnements instables ou perturbés. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés.

Le CGI est structuré selon des axes de recherche appliquée et des programmes scientifiques. Les axes de recherche appliquée sont :

  • Axe FLOWS : Flexible Logistics and Operations for sustainable WorldS dans lequel ce poste est rattaché.

  • Axe DiSCS : Digital Systems for Crisis management and Security ;

  • Axe TRACE : Territorial Resilience, Agility, and Circular Economy ;

  • Axe WHOPS : Well-being and Health through Organizational Processes and Services.

Les deux programmes scientifiques au cœur de ces axes de recherche sont :

  • HOPOPOP : Hybridization for Operations & Planning, Organizations & Performance, Optimization & Problem-solving ; 

  • AIME-DM : Automated Information Modeling and Extraction for Decision-Makers.

 

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :

Dans le contexte de l’Education 4.0, les différents acteurs d’un établissement de formation universitaire (étudiants, personnels, intervenants extérieurs, etc.) ont des contraintes et des objectifs différents ce qui rend complexe la coordination et le pilotage de tels établissements (organisation et planification des enseignements, gestion des espaces collectifs, organisation des sessions d’examens…).

En complément, ces établissements doivent s’adapter tant sur la gestion de leurs sites (meilleure adéquation à de nouvelles formes pédagogiques) que sur les flux de personnes les utilisant pour une meilleure répartition des charges et une interopérabilité de tous les outils à disposition (par exemple, un gestionnaire d’emploi du temps). Dans ce cadre, le jumeau numérique organisationnel représente le système qui permet une simulation et une aide à la prise de décision par des échanges bidirectionnels entre l’organisation physique (personnes et systèmes dont les bâtiments) et sa réplique virtuelle dans un objectif de pilotage global des flux.

Le projet DIGIFAC’Santé s’inscrit dans ce contexte. Il porte sur la conception et le développement d'un jumeau numérique des sites d’une université, de la gestion des flux étudiants et personnels et de l’évolution pédagogique de ses formations.

Un jumeau numérique ne peut remplir son rôle qu'à la condition de représenter fidèlement les informations essentielles à la prise de décision, elles-mêmes issues de données collectées dans les différents services de l’Université et des applications logicielles actuelles. Or, ces applications présentent des niveaux d’hétérogénéité différents selon leurs fonctionnalités. La nature des opérations réalisées (emploi du temps, gestion des salles et du matériel, etc.) impose des contraintes fortes sur la disponibilité de ces données : leur collecte automatique et en temps réel n'est pas toujours techniquement envisageable, ce qui constitue un défi central pour l'alimentation du jumeau numérique.

L’étude à mener dans le cadre de ce projet vise à :

Modéliser le besoin informationnel. Il s'agit de concevoir un méta-modèle capable de représenter, de façon générique et formelle, les informations strictement nécessaires à l’alimentation du jumeau numérique universitaire. Ce méta-modèle doit permettre de cadrer la remontée d'information en définissant le juste besoin, c'est-à-dire en distinguant ce qui relève de l'information décisionnelle de ce qui constitue un artefact de collecte sans valeur ajoutée pour le pilotage.

Alimenter les modèles. Une fois le méta-modèle du besoin informationnel établi, la question de son instanciation à partir de données réelles des applications existantes se pose. Comment alimenter ces modèles à partir de données hétérogènes, partielles, et produites selon des rythmes et des modalités de collecte variables ? Ceci articule des enjeux d'intégration, de qualité et de cohérence de la donnée au regard des exigences du jumeau numérique.

Gérer l'absence de certaines données. Dans un contexte où certaines opérations ne permettent pas une collecte automatique et en temps réel, en raison de la nature même des processus mis en place (par exemple, construction de l’emploi du temps, suivi des cohortes d’étudiants), comment maintenir la cohérence et la complétude de la représentation portée par le jumeau numérique ? Ce lot interroge la capacité du système à pallier les lacunes de la remontée de données par des mécanismes d'inférence ou de déduction, permettant de reconstituer un état vraisemblable du système à partir d'informations partielles.

Proposer des aides au dimensionnement et au pilotage des sites universitaires. Il s’agit ici d’utiliser le jumeau numérique dans toutes ses fonctionnalités afin entres autres de s’assurer que les évolutions bâtimentaires envisagées permettent d’accueillir l’ensemble des flux actuel et projeté pour cet établissement, de permettre d’optimiser les flux entre les différents sites et de valider les choix d’évolution des pratiques pédagogiques et leur adéquation vis à vis des capacités disponibles (salles et équipements spécifiques, surfaces, personnels,etc.).

Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables :

  • Modélisation des processus / d’organisation

  • Analyse systémique

  • Analyse de données

  • Ingénierie dirigée par les modèles

  • Aide à la décision

  • Simulation à évènements discrets et jumeau numérique

  • Fouille de processus (process mining),

  • Des connaissances en algorithmique, UML, Web sémantique seront très appréciées

Capacités et aptitudes :

  • Anglais écrit et parlé (Niveau B2 minimum exigé) ; cf. référentiel européen ; ex. :  785/990 minimum au TOEIC), attesté par une certification reconnue (TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS).

  • La maîtrise du français (C1 minimum) est exigée afin de faciliter les échanges avec les experts et les acteurs.

  • Capacité à travailler dans une équipe de recherche, autonomie, esprit d’initiative, organisation, curiosité intellectuelle…

  • Motivation pour contribuer à une application universitaire
